page: Amazon Web Services c5d.18xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8124M processor running at 3.4 GHz, delivering 72 vCPUs across 36 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled. The hardware configuration includes 144.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of an 1800 GB NVMe SSD instance store, while baseline network bandwidth is rated at 25 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates strong multi-core capabilities, scoring in the top 25% for stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, Passmark CPU, and Passmark CPU extended instructions. Read-only memory bandwidth for both small and large blocks also ranks in the top 25%. However, write operations for large blocks and single-core stress-ng performance fall into the middle 50% average tier. A notable performance tradeoff is observed in LLM text generation, where the instance scores in the bottom 25% for both small and medium models, though prompt processing remains in the average tier.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c5d.18xlarge offers high compute density and high-speed local NVMe storage, making it suitable for workloads requiring rapid scratch space and intensive CPU calculations without the overhead of network-attached storage. The strong Passmark database operations score indicates suitability for database hosting, batch processing, and multi-threaded computational tasks, whereas the weak text generation benchmarks suggest it is less optimal for real-time LLM inference.
